sources.note: Return Europe services support the reverse edges below; airport identities are cross-checked against the separate route pages. Historical frequencies are not promoted to current schedules.
The direct-flight route page identifies HKG and AMS; no weekly days are transcribed.
Air New Zealand states that it flies nonstop to Sydney Kingsford Smith (SYD) from Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch and Queenstown. Only those stated directions are used.
Air New Zealand states it offers nonstop Auckland-Perth service and separately labels Christchurch-Perth as a future December-2026 route. Only current AKL-PER is used.
Air New Zealand states it flies nonstop from Auckland to Taipei and the same page identifies arrival at Taoyuan Airport, resolving the airport as TPE without city-level airport expansion.
Air New Zealand states it offers daily nonstop Auckland to Narita service. Future Christchurch-Tokyo service is not counted on 2026-09-06.
Air New Zealand publishes AKL-CNS as nonstop with a 2026 seasonal window of March 29 through October 13. This finite current-season window is retained on the route row.

Air New Zealand's Auckland page publishes exact-code nonstop inbound routes from WLG, CHC, ZQN, DUD and IVC and also identifies current inbound international nonstop service. These directions are used independently rather than inferred from outbound services.

Current Air New Zealand Australia network page explicitly lists nonstop origin-destination pairs and distinguishes now-flying, seasonal and future routes. GCMP keeps current 2026-09-06 directions as route evidence only; no operating weekdays are inferred.

Current Air New Zealand Asia page explicitly states nonstop Auckland service to Bali, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Taipei and Tokyo. Future Christchurch services are not counted before their announced start.

Current Air New Zealand Pacific page lists nonstop Auckland routes to Rarotonga, Nadi, Niue, Apia, Nuku'alofa, Noumea and Papeete, plus seasonal Christchurch-Rarotonga. Route-only evidence does not become a dated timetable.

Current Air New Zealand USA page states nonstop Auckland service to LAX, SFO, HNL, IAH and New York. JFK is resolved by Air New Zealand's New York/Auckland pages; partner connections beyond those gateways are excluded.
Air New Zealand currently states it flies nonstop between Auckland and Vancouver. Used as bidirectional route evidence without inventing operating dates.

Air New Zealand publishes NZ1 JFK-AKL and NZ2 AKL-JFK as Air New Zealand-operated nonstop services. Used here as exact directional route/operator evidence; the legacy weekly pattern is not promoted into GCMP's dated schedule catalog.

Air India official international connectivity map says it flies nonstop to 41 destinations and draws bidirectional arrows between each listed overseas airport and the named Indian airport(s). It is a broad route-universe snapshot, not a current dated timetable; later current advisories and route launches override it where applicable.

Thai Airways' Amsterdam route publication gives exact TG936 BKK-AMS and TG937 AMS-BKK identities and a Sep-Nov 2026 travel period; its terms restrict the promotion to TG flights operated by THAI. Used as current route/operator evidence, not as a complete dated timetable.

LOT's current first-flight page explicitly calls the listed services inaugural LOT Polish Airlines flights and gives directional LOT flight identities for WAW-ALA / ALA-WAW, WAW-SFO / SFO-WAW, GDN-BRU / BRU-GDN, GDN-OSL / OSL-GDN, and KRK-ROME/MAD/BCN with their returns. Exact airport codes are accepted only where the additional airline-owned sources below resolve them.

LOT's current Almaty page explicitly identifies the year-round Warsaw (WAW)-Almaty (ALA) connection launched 2026-05-31. Combined with the directional LOT flight identities on the first-flight page; no broader Kazakhstan inference is made.
Ethiopian Airlines publishes direct ADD-MRU and MRU-ADD passenger service effective 2026-07-12 with exact ET887/ET886 identities.
Ethiopian Airlines confirms direct passenger service between ADD and ATL resumed on 2026-05-21. Used as current directional route evidence without inventing a dated schedule horizon.

Current AEGEAN Pass route inventory includes Athens to London-Heathrow as a bookable AEGEAN route. Combined with the airline's own Heathrow operations publication below to establish current route/operator evidence without inferring schedule days.
AEGEAN states it operates daily flights to London Heathrow from Athens. The current AEGEAN Pass page keeps the route live in 2026; only ATH-LHR is inserted here, with no reverse-direction inference.

AEGEAN's current flight-status board exposes exact airport pairs and distinguishes rows labeled Aegean Airlines from OlympicAir. GCMP retains only directions explicitly shown as Aegean Airlines on the reviewed current board; OA rows are excluded and no reverse direction is inferred unless separately shown.

Royal Jordanian announces a new direct route connecting Amman and Vienna effective 2026-06-24, with departures from Queen Alia International Airport. Used as current AMM-VIE directional route evidence.

Royal Jordanian's Quick Reference Timetable No.473 is explicitly valid 01Sep-30Sep 2026 and publishes exact airport codes, directional flight identities and special From/To AQJ/ADJ rows. Its legend marks one-stop services with * and RO/GF/WY-operated codeshare aircraft with #; the reviewed September flight rows contain no # marker and YYZ is the only * one-stop city row. GCMP retains only exact direct legs that can be represented without decomposing the YYZ through service.

AEGEAN's current airline trade notice states Alexandria International Airport uses HBE for travel 2026-08-08 through 2026-09-15 and changes to ALY for flights on or after 2026-09-16, with no change to flight times or flight numbers. This resolves the current airport identity for RJ515/516 without treating the September PDF's ALY label as valid for the entire month.
Oman Air announces a new direct Muscat-Abu Dhabi service starting 2026-07-09. Both directional route rows are retained without inventing a dated timetable horizon.

Oman Air announces a new direct Muscat-Sochi service starting 2026-07-02, operated year-round by Oman Air Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft. Exact directions are corroborated by the two current airport-coded route pages below.

Oman Air's current reverse-direction surface explicitly resolves Sochi (AER) to Muscat (MCT). Combined with the airline-owned direct/operator launch publication rather than inferred from the outbound direction.

Oman Air's current 2026 network-expansion release corroborates direct Sochi service from 2026-07-02 and describes a network of up to 49 destinations. The 49-destination marketing count is explicitly not used as a directional route denominator.
Croatia Airlines' current Summer-2026 timetable explicitly labels ATH-DBV and ATH-SPU as direct flights with finite operating windows, while ATH-ZAG is labeled via Dubrovnik and is excluded.

ODbL ADSBiq aircraft-diff observations from 2026-08-01 through 2026-09-06, using the public 2026-08 and 2026-09 release assets. Only exact active-alliance callsigns observed during this recent window are considered; observation alone does not provide an airport pair. Missing upstream daily assets: 2026-08-30.
CC0 standing-data exact callsign-to-route mapping. A route is retained only when the exact callsign was actually observed in the Aug 1-Sep 6 ADSBiq window.
Public search-index sitemap additionally confirms each retained physical pair remains in the current scheduled-passenger route index (65,052 directional pairs).

2026-Q2 worldwide ADS-B-derived passenger-flight observations. GCMP retains only callsign-validated directional routes with at least two known non-cargo passenger-config observations; this is recent-operation evidence, not a September timetable.

CC0 Virtual Radar Server standing-data callsign-to-route mapping at the pinned commit. Used only to corroborate the observed carrier/route identity; standing-data alone is not treated as an active timetable.

Public search-index route sitemap confirmed that each retained physical airport pair remained present in the current scheduled-passenger route index (65,052 indexed directional pairs). It does not establish the operating carrier by itself.
ODbL ADSBiq observations from 2026-08-01 through 2026-09-06 for explicitly source-backed regional/affiliate operator ICAO prefixes. Missing upstream daily assets: 2026-08-30.
CC0 exact callsign-to-route lookup used only for affiliate callsigns actually observed in the ADSBiq window.
Public route sitemap additionally confirms each retained physical pair remains in the current scheduled-passenger index (65,052 directional pairs).
BA CityFlyer: British Airways identifies BA CityFlyer as a wholly-owned subsidiary operating UK domestic and European services from London City.
BA Euroflyer: British Airways identifies BA Euroflyer as a wholly-owned subsidiary operating services from London Gatwick.
Iberia Express: Iberia states that Iberia, Iberia Express and Iberia Regional Air Nostrum jointly fly the Iberia network from Madrid.
Iberia Regional Air Nostrum: Iberia publishes dedicated guidance for flights operated by Iberia Regional Air Nostrum and applies Iberia baggage conditions.

QantasLink: Qantas conditions apply to QF-designated Australian flights operated by National Jet Systems, Sunstate or Eastern Australia; current QantasLink operations use the QLK callsign for these services.
Alliance Airlines: Qantas conditions explicitly include QF-designated Australian flights operated by Alliance Airlines.
Air Canada Rouge: Air Canada lists Air Canada Rouge as its branded operating fleet alongside Air Canada and Air Canada Express.
Aeromexico Connect: Grupo Aeromexico 2026 filing identifies Aeromexico Connect (Aerolitoral) as its operating subsidiary and regional network arm.

U.S. DOT BTS June 2026 Marketing Carrier On-Time Performance. Routes are attributed by IATA marketing carrier, so branded regional/code-share operations are assigned to AA/AS/DL/UA rather than inferred from the regional operating carrier.
Public search-index sitemap corroborates that each retained June marketing-carrier physical pair remains in the current scheduled-passenger route index (65,052 directional pairs).
CC0 callsign-to-route dictionary used as a high-recall carrier attribution candidate. A standing row can outlive active service, so it is never operating-carrier proof by itself.
Each retained physical airport pair is still present in the public current scheduled-passenger route sitemap (65,052 directional pairs). This confirms the pair, not the listed carrier identity.
